guide.title: How a complaint goes
guide.lead:
Filing is free.
You can file while still working there or after you leave.
guide.s1b: File online at the Labor Portal, or go to the regional labor office in charge of your workplace.
guide.s2b: When an inspector is assigned, you get a text or call.
guide.s3b: You and the employer each come in to check the facts. Bring the documents below.
guide.s4: Unpaid wages confirmed, order to pay
guide.s4b: If unpaid wages are confirmed, the inspector orders the employer to pay by a deadline.
guide.s5b: If the employer still does not pay, you can get a document confirming the unpaid amount.
guide.s6b: With the certificate, you can apply for the government substitute payment, where the government pays part first. Or you can get free help with a lawsuit from the Korea Legal Aid Corporation.

q1.whyBody:
At workplaces with fewer than 5 people, the law does not require extra pay for overtime, night or holiday work.
Weekly holiday pay and severance pay apply regardless of the number of workers, if you meet the other conditions.

ready.title: Things to gather
ready.lead: You can file a complaint without them. Tick the ones you have.
ready.contract.h: It's OK if you don't have one. The employer must give you a written contract (Labor Standards Act Art. 17). Messages or job ads from when you started also help.
ready.payslip.h: The employer must give you a pay slip when paying your wages (Labor Standards Act Art. 48). Photos or screenshots are fine.
ready.bank.h: Take a screenshot in your bank app of the dates and amounts paid, or print the history.
ready.time.h: Time-clock apps, transport card history, photos from work days or your own notes. Show your work calendar too.
ready.msg.h: Text messages, KakaoTalk, recordings where they promised to pay or gave you work. Do not delete them; take screenshots.
ready.id.h: Bring it when you go to the labor office. For foreign workers: residence card (외국인등록증) or passport.
ready.note:
The more evidence you have, the faster the labor inspector can check the facts.
Contact details of co-workers also help.
dj.title: Can the state pay you first?
dj.lead:
If the company does not pay, the state may pay part first.
We only tell you where to ask.
dj.paper: Did you get a 'certificate of unpaid wages' (체불임금등·사업주 확인서) from the labor office, or a court decision (such as a payment order)?
dj.year: Did you file a complaint with the labor office within 1 year from the day after you left? (2 years if you went to court)
dj.yearNow: Did you file a complaint with the labor office within 1 year from the day after your last unpaid payday? (2 years if you went to court)
dj.closed: Did the company go bankrupt, start rehabilitation, or close in practice?
dj.a.filing: Not yet, my complaint is in progress
dj.r.simple: You can look into the 'simple substitute payment' (간이대지급금). Claim it from the Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service within 6 months from the date you got the certificate (or 1 year from the date a court decision becomes final).
dj.r.filing: When your complaint ends and you get the certificate of unpaid wages, you can look into the simple substitute payment. You must claim it within 6 months from the date you got the certificate.
dj.r.first: To get the simple substitute payment, you need a certificate from the labor office or a court decision. Please file a complaint with the labor office first.
dj.r.employed: If you still work there, your ordinary hourly wage at the time must be below 1.1 times that year's minimum wage, and you can get it only once per company.
dj.r.year: If more than 1 year has passed, or you are not sure, it may be hard to get it. Please ask the Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service (1588-0075).
dj.r.closed: If the company got a bankruptcy or rehabilitation decision, or the labor office recognizes it as closed in practice, you can also look into the 'insolvency substitute payment' (도산대지급금). Claim it from the Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service within 2 years from the decision or recognition date.
dj.r.closedEmployed: The insolvency substitute payment is only for people who have left.
dj.r.company: Conditions about the company (industrial accident insurance, in business for more than 6 months) are checked by the Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service.
dj.call: Substitute payment questions (Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service)
dj.callSub: Ask if you can get it and what papers you need

words.title: Easy word list
words.lead: Tap any underlined word on the screens to see the same explanation.
words.src: Laws were checked on law.go.kr on 15 Nov 2026. This is not legal advice.
w.ordinaryWage.d: The pay you always get for your working hours: basic pay plus allowances paid in the same amount every month. Overtime, night and holiday pay are calculated from it.
w.averageWage.d: Your pay for one day: the money you got in the 3 months before leaving, divided by the number of days in that period. Severance pay is based on it. If it is lower than the ordinary wage, the ordinary wage is used.
w.weeklyHoliday.d: One paid day off a week if you worked all your set days that week. Not given if you agreed to work fewer than 15 hours a week.
w.overtime.d: Hours worked over 8 a day or 40 a week. At workplaces with 5 or more people, you get 50% extra for these hours.
w.night.d: Hours worked between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. At workplaces with 5 or more people, you get 50% extra.
w.holidayWork.d: Hours worked on a day off. At workplaces with 5 or more people: 50% extra up to 8 hours, 100% extra after 8 hours. These hours are not added again as overtime.
w.severance.d: Money you get when you leave after working 1 year or more: at least 30 days of average wage for each year. Not given for less than 1 year or under 15 hours a week.
w.minWage.d: The lowest pay per hour set by the government. In 2026 it is 10,320 won. Even if you agreed to less, you must get at least this.
w.underFive.d: A place where fewer than 5 people usually work. Extra pay for overtime, night and holiday work is not required, but wages, weekly holiday pay, severance pay and minimum wage still apply.
w.complaint.d: Telling the labor office that you were not paid so they can investigate. It is free, and you can do it while still working there or after you left. The right to claim wages ends after 3 years, so do not wait.
w.laborOffice: Regional labor office or branch office
w.laborOffice.d: A local office of the Ministry of Employment and Labor that receives and investigates complaints. The office in charge depends on your workplace address.
w.daeji.d: When the company does not pay, the state (Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service) pays part of it first and collects it from the company later.

sit.askBody:
Based on what you choose, we also calculate things like annual leave pay, dismissal notice pay and late-payment interest.
If you skip this, some money you can get may be left out.
q4.night: You work {h} hours a day between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m., so night pay is calculated too.
q6.which: Enter the money you got for the work in this month, not what you got on payday.
q6.partial: You worked until day {d} of {m}, so we calculate the monthly wage for {d} of {last} days.
result.autoDays: We assumed you worked your usual days and hours (question 4) every week and split night and overtime hours from that. Breaks were counted outside 10 p.m.–6 a.m. If your hours changed day to day, enter them in the work calendar.
cp.rawNote: This paragraph could not be polished automatically, so it is exactly as you wrote it. Tap 'Edit this paragraph' to rewrite it in formal Korean.
lt.rawNote: What happened could not be polished automatically, so it is exactly as you wrote it. Edit it on the complaint screen and make the letter again.
warn.PART_TIME_DAILY_HOURS: You work less than 40 hours a week, so daily amounts (such as annual leave pay and dismissal notice pay) use your weekly hours × 4 ÷ 20 as one day.
warn.UNDER_FIVE_EMPLOYEES: Workplaces with fewer than 5 employees do not have to pay extra rates for overtime, night or holiday work.
warn.MONTHLY_HOURS_CHECK: Your weekly hours are not 40, so the monthly base hours were calculated differently. Check this if your contract says otherwise.
warn.OVER_FORTY_HOURS: Only up to 40 hours a week count as regular hours. Hours above that are overtime: enter them, or use the work calendar, to get overtime pay.
warn.PROBATION_MIN_WAGE: During the first 3 months of probation, the employer may pay 90% of the minimum wage, so those days were compared with 90%.
warn.MIN_WAGE_UNKNOWN: The minimum wage for that year is not known, so that year was not compared with the minimum wage.
warn.BELOW_MINIMUM_WAGE: In some months you were paid less than the minimum wage.
warn.MIN_WAGE_OTHER_MONTHS: Months you did not enter were also below the minimum wage. Add them as unpaid months to include the difference.
warn.SEVERANCE_ORDINARY_WAGE: Your average daily wage was lower than your ordinary daily wage, so severance was calculated with the ordinary daily wage.
warn.DISMISSAL_CHECK: If you were dismissed because of a natural disaster or because you seriously harmed the company on purpose, you may not get this pay.
warn.ANNUAL_LEAVE_CHECK: This assumes you came to work at least 80% of the time and counts only leave from the last year. Please check.
warn.SHUTDOWN_CHECK: You get this only when you stopped work because of the company. The amount is an estimate.
warn.DELAY_INTEREST_CHECK: Late-payment interest is an estimate. It changes with the actual dates.
warn.PROBATION_FULL_MIN_WAGE: If the contract is shorter than 1 year or the job is simple labor, the full minimum wage must be paid even on probation.
warn.DAILY_RECORDS: For months with daily records, overtime, night and holiday hours were split from those records.
warn.PAID_MORE: In some months you got more than the amount due. Check that the money was for the work in that month.
